questions.question: The accounting equation states that:
options: Assets equal owner's equity plus liabilities
Assets equal owner's equity minus liabilities
Liabilities equal assets plus owner's equity
Owner's equity equals assets plus liabilities

questions.question: On which side of a ledger account do assets increase?
options: The credit side, on the right
The debit side, on the left
Either side, depending on the month
Assets never increase inside ledger accounts

questions.question: The double-entry principle requires that every transaction:
options: Is recorded twice in the same account
Is approved by the owner in writing
Touches at least two accounts, with total debits equal to total credits
Increases at least one asset

subtopics.title: Transactions (a) and (b) — Capital and a Cash Asset Swap

questions.question: R. Naidoo deposits R80 000 as capital. The double entry is:
options: Debit Capital R80 000, credit Bank R80 000
Debit Bank R80 000, credit Drawings R80 000
Debit Vehicles R80 000, credit Capital R80 000
Debit Bank R80 000, credit Capital R80 000

questions.question: The business buys a scooter for R24 000 cash. The effect on the accounting equation is:
options: Assets rise and fall by R24 000 — net effect nil; O and L unchanged
Assets up R24 000 and liabilities up R24 000
Assets down R24 000 and owner's equity down R24 000
No entries are needed because nothing changed

questions.question: Why must the R24 000 asset swap still be recorded with two entries?
options: Because the bank demands a record of all swaps
Because Vehicles increased and Bank decreased — two real changes, each needing its entry
Because owner's equity secretly changed
Because asset swaps are recorded once in each journal

questions.question: Trading stock of R15 000 is bought on credit. The double entry is:
options: Debit Creditors Control R15 000, credit Trading Stock R15 000
Debit Trading Stock R15 000, credit Bank R15 000
Debit Trading Stock R15 000, credit Creditors Control R15 000
Debit Bank R15 000, credit Creditors Control R15 000

questions.question: The equation effect of the R15 000 credit purchase is:
options: A up R15 000, L up R15 000, O unchanged
A up R15 000, O up R15 000, L unchanged
A unchanged, L up R15 000, O down R15 000
A down R15 000, L down R15 000, O unchanged

questions.question: The business pays a creditor R6 000. The double entry is:
options: Debit Bank R6 000, credit Creditors Control R6 000
Debit Creditors Control R6 000, credit Trading Stock R6 000
Debit Trading Stock R6 000, credit Bank R6 000
Debit Creditors Control R6 000, credit Bank R6 000

questions.question: After the R6 000 payment, the effect on the equation is:
options: Both A and L fall by R6 000 — the equation stays level
A falls R6 000 and O falls R6 000
Only L falls; assets are unaffected
The equation is out of balance until month end

questions.question: After all four transactions, total assets of Naidoo Stationers are:
After the four transactions, owner's equity plus liabilities equals:
options: R80 000 plus R9 000, which is R89 000 — matching total assets
R80 000 plus R15 000, which is R95 000
R80 000 minus R9 000, which is R71 000
R89 000 plus R9 000, which is R98 000

questions.question: Wages of R1 800 are paid. The correct analysis is:
options: Debit Bank R1 800; credit Wages R1 800
Debit Capital R1 800; credit Bank R1 800
Debit Wages R1 800; credit Bank R1 800 — an expense reducing owner's equity
Debit Wages R1 800; credit Capital R1 800

questions.question: In the two-pocket picture, everything a business owns was paid for by:
options: The own-money pocket or the owed-money pocket — there is no third source
The bank, in all cases
Profit made in earlier years only
The government or the owner

questions.question: The three piles — owned things, the owner's pocket, the owed pocket — carry the accounting names:
options: Income, expenses, profit
Assets, owner's equity, liabilities
Debits, credits, balances
Capital, drawings, bank

questions.question: When the books balance, they confirm that:
options: The business made a profit this month
All creditors have been paid in full
The owner took no drawings
No rand appeared from nowhere and none vanished into nowhere

subtopics.title: Four Moves on the Kitchen Table

questions.question: Move two — the R24 000 scooter bought for cash — leaves the table level because:
options: No entries were made for it
The owed pile rose while the owned pile fell
Two moves inside the owned pile cancel: scooter in, bank money out
The owner's pocket absorbed the difference

questions.question: In move three, R15 000 of stock arrives on credit. Which piles move?
options: Owned up R15 000 and owed up R15 000, together
Owned up R15 000 and owner's pocket up R15 000
Owed up R15 000 only
Owned down R15 000 and owed down R15 000

questions.question: The table staying level through all four moves is a picture of:
options: The business breaking even
Double entry — every move touches two places equally
The owner investing more capital
The petty cash float being restored

questions.question: The one question that unlocks every transaction is:
options: How much profit did this make?
Which journal does this belong to?
Who authorised this payment?
Which two places, and which way?

questions.question: Expenses sit on the debit side because they:
options: Shrink the owner's pocket — they reduce owner's equity
Increase assets
Increase liabilities
Are paid in cash

questions.question: R1 800 wages are paid. In table language, the two places and directions are:
options: Owned pile up; owed pile up
Owned pile down; owner's pocket down through the Wages expense
Owed pile down; owner's pocket up
Owner's pocket up; owned pile down
